# Intake Brief — End of Turn summary dialog for competitive mode (MS-0MVO1SFCM000ZLBI)

## Problem statement

The single-player End of Turn summary dialog (MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41) gives the
player a deliberate review-and-advance moment after each turn. Competitive
(human-vs-AI) play has no equivalent: after the shared day's closing
presentation (`presentCompetitiveClosing`) the day auto-advances with only the
transient per-seat income text (`Player 1: +X coins | Player 2: +Y coins`, via
`perSeatClosingSummary`) and the incident reveal. There is no moment to compare
each seat's standing for the round just completed — businesses owned, income
and expenses per seat. This item extends the End of Turn summary dialog to
competitive mode: one panel per completed round (one shared day where every
seat finished and the closing ran), with **owner-keyed rows** (businesses
owned, income/expenses per seat).

## Users

- **Main Street competitive player (human seat)** — plays week-by-week against
  AI seats on the shared street; after each shared day's animations finish,
  wants a persistent panel showing every seat's round result and a deliberate
  "start the next day" action (parity with the single-player dialog).

**User stories:**

- As a competitive player, when the shared day's closing animations finish, I
  see one panel summarising the round with a row per seat (businesses owned,
  income, expenses, net change, closing coins/reputation/score) so I can
  compare standings and learn from the round.
- As a competitive player, I click **[ Next Turn ]** to start the next shared
  day — the day does not advance until I do.
- As a competitive player, I see the same (disabled) **[ Bank Loan ]**
  affordance as the single-player dialog, so the loans option is planned and
  consistent across modes.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. In competitive play (N ≥ 2), after the shared closing presentation completes, a Turn Summary dialog appears with one panel per completed round — one owner-keyed row per non-eliminated seat showing businesses owned, income (with the per-phase breakdown), ongoing expenses per category (staff / community / business), net coin change, and closing coins / reputation / score; the next shared day does **not** start until the player clicks **[ Next Turn ]**, and reduced-motion, replay and headless/AI-driven paths skip the dialog and keep the existing auto-advance pacing.
2. The dialog content is **engine-computed and owner-keyed**: the competitive close surfaces per-seat ongoing costs, businesses owned and net change on `TurnResult` (extending the parent item's owner-keyed ledger design), so every value shown is testable without a browser and consistent with the single-player ledger; additions are optional and backwards-compatible — `MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn`, `presentCompetitiveClosing` and the headless/Monte-Carlo paths are unaffected when the field is absent.
3. The dialog reuses the single-player Turn Summary presentation: the Phaser-free model renders owner-keyed rows (reusing the competitive scoreboard's `You`/`AI n` labels and `resolveSeatColour` seat colours); **[ Next Turn ]** (primary) and **[ Bank Loan ]** (**disabled** with an explanatory hint, behind the same single wiring seam that MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG replaces — never enabled by this item) buttons; overlay conventions: `createOverlayBackground` / `createOverlayButton`, elements in `s.hudContainer`, depths 199/200/201, pushed into `s.overlayObjects`, `safePlaySound` for the button SFX.
4. Single-player behaviour is unchanged; the competitive gate slots only in the scene presentation tail — between `presentCompetitiveClosing` completing and `startTurnPhase` in `presentCompetitiveDayTail` — and never in the engine/headless close path; checkpoint save ordering (`presentCompetitiveDayTail` saves before the closing) is unchanged, and the dialog adds no save and mutates no state.
5. At least one automated test per surfaced value (Phaser-free model tests for owner-keyed rows, engine per-seat ledger tests, and a competitive-mode browser dialog test); **all related documentation is updated** (docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md competitive closing and end-of-turn summary sections, plus any README/dev references); **the full project test suite passes** with the changes.

## Constraints

- **Blocked-by MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41** (outbound dependency): the parent item is
  still `open` (stage `intake_complete`) — its `TurnResult` owner-keyed ledger
  does **not exist in the code yet**. This item builds on and consumes that
  ledger; implementers must land/coordinate with the parent first. Per-seat
  expense capture does not exist anywhere today — `applyCompetitiveOngoingCosts`
  returns `void` and only logs — so the per-seat ledger extension is real
  engine work on top of the parent's ledger shape (kept optional and
  backwards-compatible throughout).
- Presentation-only contract: the dialog reads committed state / `result` and
  never mutates engine state or consumes RNG. In competitive, deltas are
  already applied to each `PlayerRecord` before the closing is presented, so
  the panel shows post-round values; the checkpoint save stays in
  `presentCompetitiveDayTail` (existing ordering).
- Overlay conventions (AGENTS.md UI best practices) exactly as the parent
  item constrains: `createOverlayBackground` + `createOverlayButton` from
  `@ui`; elements parented into `s.hudContainer`; depths 199 / 200 / 201;
  everything pushed into `s.overlayObjects` for dismissal; instant appearance
  (reduced-motion safe); button SFX via `safePlaySound`.
- Headless determinism and bounded pacing must not regress: Monte-Carlo /
  AI headless days (`MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts`, `MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn`)
  never invoke the scene presentation and must never show/block on the dialog;
  the competitive closing bound (`COMPETITIVE_CLOSING_MAX_TOTAL_MS`) stays.
- **Assumption (Q-scope, from repo evidence):** a "round" equals **one
  completed shared day** — all non-eliminated seats finished and the shared
  closing ran. The engine has no separate "round" concept beyond the shared
  day (`round-robin` seat iteration only), so "one panel per completed round"
  = one dialog per shared day.
- **Assumption (blocking safety):** competitive is human-vs-AI on one device
  (no networked multiplayer), so a blocking dialog gated on the single human
  seat cannot stall other humans. Interactive Q1 = A.
- The parent item's banking-hint ordering assumption is single-player-only and
  does not apply to the competitive panel (no banking-hint step exists in the
  competitive closing).
- `TurnResult` / `OwnerIncomeResult` additions must not break competitive
  callers (`MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn`, `presentCompetitiveClosing`,
  `perSeatClosingSummary`, scoreboard/HUD consumers) — keep ledger fields
  optional/absent-undefined-safe and guard with tests.

## Existing state

- `endCompetitiveTurnDay` (`src/MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts`):
  ends the human's MarketPhase, drives AI seats to the shared closing, runs
  `runCompetitiveClosing`, then `presentCompetitiveDayTail` →
  station checkpoint save → `presentCompetitiveClosing(closing, () =>
  startTurnPhase())`. The new gate slots at the end of the closing
  presentation, before `startTurnPhase` (presentation path only).
- `TurnResult.playerIncome?: OwnerIncomeResult[]` **already exists**
  (`src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts`): owner-keyed income, non-eliminated seats,
  in seat order, populated by `applyCompetitiveIncome`
  (`src/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts`, through `resolveCompetitiveClosingPhases`
  in `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts`). Each entry carries
  `income.phaseBreakdown.perSlotBreakdown` (base / synergy / reputation /
  events / upcoming slots per owner).
- Per-seat ongoing costs are computed in `applyCompetitiveOngoingCosts`
  (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts`) — staff salaries per owner, community +
  business running costs per slot owner via `ownerTaggedGrid` — but are
  **not surfaced** on any result (void, log-only). Businesses owned per seat
  are derivable from `ownerTaggedGrid` / `getSlotOwnerId`
  (`src/MainStreetAdjacencyOwner.ts`).
- Per-seat row conventions exist in `buildCompetitiveScoreboard`
  (`src/scenes/MainStreetCompetitiveScoreboard.ts`): `You` / `AI n` labels,
  `resolveSeatColour` seat colours, coin/rep/score columns — reused by the
  Game Over overlay model `MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts`.
- Overlay precedent and single-player dialog model come from
  MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41 (its `MainStreetTurnSummary` model +
  `showTurnSummaryDialog`); docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md documents the
  competitive closing presentation (section "Competitive phase-major closing
  presentation …"), including the current auto-advance behaviour that this
  item changes.

## Desired change

1. Engine: capture and surface the per-seat round ledger on `TurnResult` —
   per-owner ongoing expenses (staff / community / business), businesses
   owned, net coin change — extending the `OwnerIncomeResult` shape (or the
   parent's owner-keyed ledger) inside `resolveCompetitiveClosingPhases` /
   `applyCompetitiveOngoingCosts`; keep everything optional so
   single-player, N=1 and headless calls are untouched.
2. Model: extend the single-player Phaser-free `MainStreetTurnSummary` to
   render **owner-keyed competitive rows** (seat label + colour from the
   competitive scoreboard conventions) for the round just closed.
3. UI: extend the single-player `showTurnSummaryDialog(...)` (or a thin
   competitive sibling sharing the same panel) with **[ Next Turn ]**
   (primary) and a **disabled [ Bank Loan ]** button behind the shared wiring
   seam; gate `presentCompetitiveDayTail` so the deferred
   (animations-enabled) path presents the dialog when the closing completes
   and only calls `startTurnPhase` after **[ Next Turn ]** — reduced-motion /
   replay / headless keep today's auto-advance.
4. Tests and docs: Phaser-free model tests, engine per-seat ledger tests, a
   competitive browser dialog test; update docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md
   (competitive closing + end-of-turn summary sections).

## Key Files:

- `src/MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts` — gate `presentCompetitiveDayTail` on the dialog (between closing-complete and `startTurnPhase`); presentation path only
- `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts` — `resolveCompetitiveClosingPhases` / `finishCompetitiveClosingTail`: surface the per-seat round ledger on `TurnResult`
- `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` — `applyCompetitiveOngoingCosts`: return/capture the per-owner expense breakdown (staff / community / business)
- `src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts` — extend `TurnResult` (and/or `OwnerIncomeResult`) with the optional owner-keyed round ledger (expenses, businesses owned, net change)
- `src/MainStreetAdjacency.ts` / `src/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts` — `OwnerIncomeResult` shape extension
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts` — extend the Phaser-free summary model to render owner-keyed competitive rows (reusing scoreboard label/colour conventions)
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` + `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — dialog presentation + delegation (shared with the single-player panel); `createOverlayBackground` / `createOverlayButton` per overlay conventions
- `src/scenes/MainStreetCompetitiveScoreboard.ts` — reuse `You` / `AI n` labels, `resolveSeatColour` colours for rows
- Docs: `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` (competitive closing + end-of-turn summary sections)
- Tests: `tests/main-street/turn-summary-competitive-model.test.ts` (pure model), `tests/main-street/competitive-turn-ledger.test.ts` (engine), `tests/main-street/turn-summary-dialog.browser.test.ts` (competitive overlay)

## Related work

### Automated related-work report (`find_related.py`)

- **MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41** – End of Turn summary dialog (single-player seed)
  (open)
- **MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG** – Bank Loans (open)
- **MS-0MUWD9C1A004JZVQ** – Refactor end-of-turn presentation: remove
  single-player/competitive duplication and add per-seat income feedback
  (completed)
- Repository matches: `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `core/AGENTS.md`,
  `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (keyword overlap: competitive,
  ledger, end-of-turn, dialog, seat, round, businesses).
- Duplicate check: `wl search "turn summary competitive"` returned only the
  parent, the deferred Bank Loans seam and End of game stats — **no
  overlapping completed item**; no duplicate/partial-overlap rewrite needed.

### Hand-curated context

- `MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41` — **parent / blocked-by**: single-player End of Turn
  summary dialog + `TurnResult` owner-keyed ledger; this item's panel consumes
  that ledger and the parent's overlay/model. Not yet implemented (open,
  intake_complete) — ordering constraint.
- `MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG` — **Bank Loans**: the seam this item's disabled Bank
  Loan button exposes; enablement blocked by that item (shared with
  single-player panel).
- `MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV` — **End of game stats** (open, low): turn-by-turn
  history + graphs on Game Over; consumes the same per-turn ledger data
  (synergy, not duplication — distinct screen).
- `MS-0MUWD9C1A004JZVQ` (completed) — end-of-turn presentation refactor:
  source of today's `closingSummary` / shared closing primitive.
- `MS-0MUXAQQON006XA6I` + `MS-0MUYFXA36009EMH0` (completed) — competitive
  per-seat income choreography and per-seat animated closing: the cadence this
  panel extends; `TurnResult.playerIncome` originates here.
- `MS-0MUWDL0V40041USM` (completed) — game-over overlay epic: the
  Phaser-free-model + overlay-convention precedent (`MainStreetGameOverSummary`
  reusing `buildCompetitiveScoreboard`).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (round = day):** "one panel per completed round" maps to one
  panel per completed shared day (every seat finished + closing ran); the
  engine has no separate round concept. Recorded from repo evidence; if a
  day-vs-round distinction exists conceptually (e.g. a preset defining round
  length), the panel cadence would need revisiting — flagged for implementer
  verification.
- **Assumption (single human seat):** competitive is human-vs-AI on one
  device, so a blocking dialog on the human's **[ Next Turn ]** cannot stall
  other humans; multifloored safety holds for the current product shape.
  (If networked multiplayer ever lands, blocking semantics need a per-seat
  pause protocol.)
- **Risk (parent not landed):** the owner-keyed ledger this item consumes does
  not exist yet; if the parent lands without the per-seat expense capture
  (today `void`/log-only), this item must extend it — keep additions optional
  and guarded so `presentCompetitiveClosing` and headless/Monte-Carlo flows are
  byte-stable when absent.
- **Risk (blocking regresses headless pacing):** the gate must live in the
  scene presentation tail only (`presentCompetitiveDayTail`), never in engine
  close functions; Monte-Carlo / AI headless days never touch the scene and
  must continue to auto-advance under `COMPETITIVE_CLOSING_MAX_TOTAL_MS`.
- **Risk (eliminated seats):** the closing already omits eliminated seats from
  `playerIncome`; the panel must render exactly the seats the closing surfaced
  (no ghost rows for bankrupt/eliminated seats) and say so in its test.
- **Risk (loans are per-owner):** the shared disabled Bank Loan seam is a
  single hook today; when MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG lands, competitive loans are
  likely per-seat — keep the seam shaped so it can become
  `onBankLoanAction(seatId)` without re-plumbing the panel.
- **Scope-creep risk:** per-round history across days (post-game stats,
  MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV), networked multiplayer, live loans
  (MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG) and any round-summary log/graph features are outside
  this item; tracked as linked items, not scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Blocking behaviour — in single-player the dialog blocks the next-day
  advance until [ Next Turn ] is clicked; in competitive the day currently
  auto-advances after the closing presentation. Options: A) Block like
  single-player — next day starts only after [ Next Turn ]. B) Non-blocking —
  panel appears but the day advances behind it / auto-dismisses."
  — Answer (operator): "A". Source: interactive reply, intake session
  MS-0MVO1SFCM000ZLBI, 2026-10-25. (Recommended option was A — consistency
  with the single-player dialog; accepted as chosen.)
- Q2: "Per-seat data source — per-seat expenses aren't captured anywhere
  today (TurnResult.playerIncome covers income only). Options: A) Extend the
  engine with an owner-keyed per-seat ledger on TurnResult (per-seat ongoing
  costs, businesses owned, net change — engine-computed, testable headless),
  mirroring the parent's ledger. B) Derive presentation-only at panel time
  from committed state."
  — Answer (operator): "A". Source: interactive reply, intake session
  MS-0MVO1SFCM000ZLBI, 2026-10-25. (Recommended option was A — matches the
  parent item's owner-keyed ledger design intent; accepted as chosen.)
- Q3: "Bank Loan button parity — the single-player dialog renders a disabled
  [ Bank Loan ] button with a wiring seam for MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG. Options:
  A) Same disabled Bank Loan button in the competitive panel (parity).
  B) Omit it — strictly the seed's content."
  — Answer (operator): "A". Source: interactive reply, intake session
  MS-0MVO1SFCM000ZLBI, 2026-10-25. (Recommended option was A — one shared
  loans seam avoids divergent affordances; accepted as chosen.)

# Intake brief: Remove broken `scaffold:game`/`scaffold:games` npm scripts from generated game repos

**Type:** chore · **Priority:** low · **Cross-repo:** yes (Tableau-Card-Engine core via the `./core` submodule) · **Discovered-from:** MS-0MVK4TS31000YNFL

## Problem statement

Every generated game repo (`tce-main-street`, `tce-golf`, `tce-blackjack`, …) declares two npm scripts — `scaffold:game` and `scaffold:games` — that point at `tsx scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`, a file that does **not** exist in a game repo (Option C: game repos have no root `scripts/` tree; the scaffold lives in the core at `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`). Invoking either script fails with a module-not-found error. The working game-repo entry point, `npm run scaffold`, passes `--core-root ./core` and exists in every generated repo.

Root cause (resolved): `renderPackageJson` in `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` inherits the **entire** core `scripts` map from the core manifest (line ~280: `...Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(manifest.scripts ?? {}))`). `core/package.json` legitimately declares `scaffold:game`/`scaffold:games` for core-repo use, so both leak unmodified into every generated game repo. The description's open "which is true" question is answered: the template **does** emit them, but only by inheritance — the fix is a template-side filter, not merely deleting two lines from each repo.

## Users

- **Game-repo maintainers (agents and humans)** — run npm scripts inside a game repo without tripping over dead entries.
  - *User story:* "As a maintainer of tce-main-street, I want `npm run scaffold:game` to either work or not be declared, so a script listed in my repo never fails with module-not-found."
- **Core scaffold owners (Tableau-Card-Engine)** — keep the template emitting only what a game repo can actually run.
  - *User story:* "As a core template owner, I want the scaffold to filter core-only scripts (including any future ones) out of generated repos, so a re-scaffold never reintroduces broken entries."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **This repo's `package.json` no longer declares `scaffold:game` or `scaffold:games`.** `npm run scaffold` remains and resolves to `tsx ./core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts --game main-street ...`. # Per-turn loan repayment in the closing sequence

Parent: MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG (Bank Loans). Depends on the loan model slice.

## Goal

As a player holding a loan, exactly `perTurnRepayment` coins leave my wallet at the end of
every turn for `termTurns` turns, the deduction shows up in the turn's net summary as an
expense, and the loan then disappears.

## Context

- Turn economy closes in `processEndOfTurn` (`src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`): income,
  staff/community/business ongoing costs, then the incident, then `appendTurnNetRow`.
  Repayment belongs in that same sequence so the net row reflects it.
- Turn net rows are written by `appendTurnNetRow` (delta summary + totals lines) and the
  `TurnResult` carries an optional `turnLedger` (MS-0MVP45KZV006TMUK) with one-off deltas —
  prefer extending that ledger so the Turn Summary dialog can surface the expense rather
  than adding a parallel channel.
- Competitive seats keep their wallet in `state.players[].coins` with
  `state.resourceBank` as the working mirror (`bindCompetitiveSeat` /
  `restoreCompetitiveSeat`); single-player has no `state.players`. Repayment must work for
  whichever wallet is active, and must not disturb the other seats in a competitive close.
- Producer Q6=A: repayment is deducted unconditionally — a shortfall leaves `coins < 0` and
  the ordinary bankruptcy path decides what happens next. The bailout offer itself is the
  next slice; this slice must not add an offer.

## Desired change

1. `applyLoanRepayments(state)` in `src/MainStreetLoans.ts`: for each active loan, debit
   `perTurnRepayment` through the ledger/wallet path, decrement `turnsRemaining`, remove the
   loan when `turnsRemaining` reaches 0, and log a one-off expense row.
2. Call it in `processEndOfTurn` after the incident resolution and **before** the
   end-condition checks, for both the deferred and the legacy paths, and include the
   repayment in the pending/turn ledger deltas.
3. Keep `loansEnabled: false` a hard no-op (no log rows, no ledger entries) so the headless
   baseline stays byte-identical.
4. Tests: three-turn schedule for 600/6 (110 per turn, 660 total), retirement after
   `termTurns` (no seventh deduction), ledger/net-row expense entry, unclamped deduction
   leaving `coins < 0`, and a loans-disabled no-op.

## Acceptance Criteria

- At the end of every turn in which a seat holds an active loan, exactly `perTurnRepayment` coins are deducted from that seat's wallet and the deduction is recorded in the turn's net summary as a one-off expense.
- The loan is retired after `termTurns` payments and no further deductions occur.
- Repayment is deducted unconditionally: a payment that exceeds the seat's balance leaves coins < 0 and triggers the normal bankruptcy path, so a seat already repaying a loan receives no new bailout offer.

## Key Files:

- `src/MainStreetLoans.ts` — `applyLoanRepayments` and repayment logging
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — call site ahead of the end-condition checks, ledger wiring
- `src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts` — repayment line on `TurnResult.turnLedger`
- `src/MainStreetStateLog.ts` — activity-log helper (if a new effect class is needed)
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetLoanBailout.test.ts` — new repayment tests

# Bankruptcy bailout offer, AI policy and headless resolution

Parent: MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG (Bank Loans). Depends on the takeLoan command and repayment
slices.

## Goal

When a seat would go bankrupt with no active loan, the run does not end: the seat is
offered a loan instead, may accept (principal credited, play continues) or decline
(today's bankruptcy), while an AI seat auto-accepts the largest option and headless runs
never stall.

## Context

- Bankruptcy is currently terminal in two places in `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`:
  `checkImmediateLoss` (single-player, `coins < 0` → `endReason 'bankruptcy'`) and
  `resolveCompetitiveSeatFailures` (competitive seats). This slice handles the
  **single-player** path; competitive parity is the next slice.
- The established pending-decision pattern is `state.pendingEventChoice` /
  `state.pendingPiggyback`: the closing pauses (returns `choicePending` /
  `piggybackPending` with `requiresDeferredClosing`), the UI resolves the decision, then the
  closing tail re-runs. `state.pendingLoanOffer` must follow the same shape, with a
  `pendingLoanOffer` flag on `TurnResult`.
- Ordering matters: the bailout intercept must run **before** `checkImmediateLoss` /
  `checkEndConditions`, and must respect `applyFirstSharedDaySolvencyGrace`
  (MS-0MVJNFESC005QJ41 — no player is bankrupt on the opening day).
- Producer decisions: Q3=A (bailout only, no proactive AI lending), Q5=A (AI auto-accepts
  the **largest** option), Q6=A (shortfall unconditional). At most one offer per seat per
  turn — a decline must converge to game over in a single pass, never loop.
- Headless: `endTurnHeadless` (`src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`) and the Monte Carlo
  runner must resolve a pending offer deterministically with the AI policy; they must never
  leave a pending pause open.

## Desired change

1. `maybeOfferBailout(state)` in `src/MainStreetLoans.ts`: when the acting seat is at
   `coins < 0`, holds no active loan, loans are enabled and no offer has already been made
   this turn, set `pendingLoanOffer = { ownerId, reason: 'bankruptcy', options }` and return
   "pause" so the closing defers instead of declaring the loss.
2. `acceptLoanOffer(state, option)` / `declineLoanOffer(state)` resolve the pending offer
   (accept runs the `takeLoan` path, decline clears the offer and lets the loss declaration
   stand), then the caller re-runs/completes the closing tail exactly once.
3. `TurnResult` gains `pendingLoanOffer` (mirroring `choicePending` / `piggybackPending`),
   and the per-turn "already offered" guard so a second evaluation in the same turn cannot
   re-offer.
4. AI/headless: auto-accept the largest option (deterministic tie-break: largest principal,
   then longest term) in the AI and headless paths; no proactive loans anywhere.
5. Tests: offer on bankruptcy with no loan, accept credits principal and play continues,
   decline → bankruptcy, second offer in the same turn suppressed, AI largest-option
   auto-accept and AI survival (not eliminated), shortfall with an active loan → bankruptcy
   without an offer, headless determinism (no stalled pending offer), first-turn grace
   respected.

## Acceptance Criteria

- When a seat would fail on coins < 0 in single-player play and holds no active loan, the game does not end: a loan offer is presented instead, accepting credits the principal and play continues, while declining preserves today's bankruptcy behaviour.
- At most one bailout offer is made per seat per turn (no offer loop), and a seat that already holds an active loan preserves today's bankruptcy behaviour.
- An AI seat that hits coins < 0 with no active loan auto-accepts the largest loan option and is not eliminated, and AI seats take no proactive (non-bailout) loans.
- Headless turn execution never stalls on a pending loan offer and resolves deterministically using the AI bailout policy.
- Unit tests cover bailout offer/accept/decline, shortfall → bankruptcy and the AI largest-option policy.

## Key Files:

- `src/MainStreetLoans.ts` — `maybeOfferBailout`, `acceptLoanOffer`, `declineLoanOffer`
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — intercept before `checkImmediateLoss`, deferred-closing pause/resume
- `src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts` — `pendingLoanOffer` on `TurnResult`
- `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — AI bailout auto-accept (largest option)
- `src/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — headless resolution of a pending offer
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetLoanBailout.test.ts` — new bailout/AI/headless tests

# Competitive seat bailout parity

Parent: MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG (Bank Loans). Depends on the single-player bailout slice.

## Goal

In competitive mode an unlucky week must not knock a seat out: a seat at `coins < 0` with
no active loan is offered the same bailout as in single-player, while a seat already
repaying a loan is eliminated exactly as today.

## Context

- Competitive failure handling lives in `resolveCompetitiveSeatFailures`
  (`src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`): a human failure ends the game, AI failures call
  `eliminateCompetitiveSeat` and `checkLastStanding` then decides a last-standing win
  (MS-0MUVQRBVI0015AB2). The bailout intercept must run **before** those declarations, so
  an AI survives a bailout and a last-standing win is delayed accordingly.
- Competitive closings are driven from `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts`
  (`processEndOfTurn` call sites, `appendTurnNetRow`, agent-choice pausing). A per-seat
  pending offer must pause the closing the same way the event-choice pause does, and the
  offer must be attributed to the failing seat (`ownerId`), not the acting seat globally.
- Per-seat wallets: `state.players[].coins` with `state.resourceBank` as the mirror for the
  active seat (`bindCompetitiveSeat` / `restoreCompetitiveSeat`). A bailout for a non-active
  seat must credit that seat's wallet and leave the working mirror consistent.
- Producer Q3=A / Q5=A: the AI seat auto-accepts the largest option; no proactive AI
  lending. Q6=A: a seat already holding an active loan is eliminated as today.

## Desired change

1. Extend `maybeOfferBailout` to evaluate every seat at failure evaluation time (not just
   the acting seat), creating at most one pending offer per seat per turn.
2. Intercept `resolveCompetitiveSeatFailures` (and its `checkCompetitiveEndConditions`
   caller) so an offer-eligible seat is removed from the failure list and the game/elimination
   is not declared; ineligible seats keep today's behaviour.
3. Resolve AI offers inline via the AI policy; leave a human seat's offer pending for the UI,
   and continue the competitive closing after resolution.
4. Integration test: competitive run where an AI seat hits `coins < 0`, receives the largest
   loan, stays in the game and is not eliminated; a seat already holding a loan is still
   eliminated; a declining human seat still ends the run with `endReason 'bankruptcy'`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- When a competitive seat would fail on coins < 0 and holds no active loan, the game does not end (and the seat is not eliminated): a loan offer is presented instead, accepting credits the principal and play continues.
- An AI seat that already holds an active loan is eliminated exactly as today, and declining the offer preserves today's bankruptcy behaviour for a human seat.
- The competitive-seat path is covered by an integration test proving the bailout runs before elimination and last-standing checks.

## Key Files:

- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — `resolveCompetitiveSeatFailures` intercept
- `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts` — competitive closing pause/resume
- `src/MainStreetLoans.ts` — per-seat offer evaluation and wallet handling
- `src/MainStreetEngine.ts` — public exports
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetLoanCompetitive.test.ts` — new competitive integration test

# Bailout overlay UI and deferred closing resume

Parent: MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG (Bank Loans). Depends on the single-player bailout slice.

## Goal

When a bailout offer is open, the player sees a dialog listing the loan options with their
per-turn and total repayment plus a Decline button, and accepting or declining resumes the
turn exactly once.

## Context

- Overlay conventions: `createOverlayBackground` / `createOverlayButton` from `@ui`, all
  elements parented into `s.hudContainer`, depths 199/200/201, every object pushed into
  `s.overlayObjects`, `safePlaySound` for SFX, reduced-motion safe instant appearance.
- Precedents: `showEventChoiceDialog` / `showPiggybackDialog` /
  `showTurnSummaryDialog` in `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts`, delegated from
  `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts`; pure Phaser-free models such as
  `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts` (`MainStreetTurnSummary.ts` is the newest
  example) keep the content testable without a browser.
- Resume path: the deferred closing tail is re-run from
  `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` (`finishTurnPresentation` /
  `finishDeferredTurnClosing`) — the same shape used for pending event choices.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts` must not present game-over while a bailout
  offer is open, but must present the normal bankruptcy summary after a decline.
- The Turn Summary "Bank Loan" button (`onBankLoanAction` seam in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` / `MainStreetScene.ts`) is deliberately a
  separate follow-up item — do not wire it here.

## Desired change

1. New pure model `src/scenes/MainStreetLoanOverlayModel.ts` (or equivalent) building the
   option rows from `pendingLoanOffer` + `config.loanOptions`: principal, per-turn
   repayment, total repayment, term.
2. New `src/scenes/MainStreetLoanOverlay.ts` rendering the dialog with one button per
   option and a Decline button, following the overlay conventions above.
3. Wire presentation into the turn controller: when `result.pendingLoanOffer` is set, show
   the overlay instead of the game-over summary; on resolution call the loan accept/decline
   handler and then run the deferred closing tail exactly once.
4. Tests: model test for the option rows, overlay browser test for render + button count +
   dismiss behaviour, and a turn-flow test proving the closing resumes once (no replay, no
   duplicate offer).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A bailout overlay is rendered whenever a pending loan offer exists, listing each loan option with its per-turn and total repayment plus a Decline choice.
- Accepting or declining the offer resumes the deferred closing sequence, and the game-over summary is not shown while a bailout offer is open.
- Tests assert the overlay is presented once per offer, the resume completes the closing exactly once, and no replay or duplicate-offer loop occurs.

## Key Files:

- `src/scenes/MainStreetLoanOverlay.ts` — new overlay dialog
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — dialog presentation following the event-choice pattern
- `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — delegation method
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — deferred-closing resume wiring
- `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts` — suppress game-over while an offer is open
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetLoanOverlay.test.ts` — new model/flow tests
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetLoanOverlay.browser.test.ts` — new overlay browser test

# Visible obligation: HUD readout and activity log

Parent: MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG (Bank Loans). Depends on the takeLoan command and repayment
slices.

## Goal

The debt burden is never hidden: taking a loan writes it to the activity log (amount,
per-turn repayment, term) and the HUD shows the remaining obligation (turns left and
per-turn amount) beside the coin/reputation readouts.

## Context

- Single-player HUD: `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts` (coin / reputation readouts and
  their layout anchors). Competitive HUD: `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererCompetitiveHud.ts`
  plus `src/scenes/MainStreetCompetitiveScoreboard.ts` for per-seat rows.
- Activity log rows are written through `addLog` (`src/MainStreetStateLog.ts`) with an
  effect classification (`neutral` / gain / loss style helpers) — reuse it rather than
  adding a new channel.
- Layout anchors are covered by `tests/main-street/MainStreetLayoutAnchors.browser.test.ts`
  and HUD text by `tests/main-street/MainStreet-hud-week.browser.test.ts` and
  `tests/main-street/MainStreetCompetitiveHud.browser.test.ts`; new HUD text needs the same
  kind of assertion so it cannot silently disappear or overlap.
- Use UK English in player-facing copy (e.g. "Loan: 110 coins/turn, 4 turns left").

## Desired change

1. Log rows: on acceptance, a loan row with principal, per-turn repayment and term; on each
   repayment, an expense row (already added by the repayment slice — extend rather than
   duplicate).
2. HUD: an active-loan readout showing turns left and per-turn repayment for the human seat
   (single-player) and for each seat holding a loan (competitive scoreboard), placed beside
   the coin/reputation readouts without overlapping existing anchors.
3. Hide the readout entirely when no loan is active or `loansEnabled` is false.
4. Tests: activity-log rows for acceptance and repayment, HUD readout text/visibility
   (single-player and competitive), and no readout when there is no loan.

## Acceptance Criteria

- While a loan is active the player can see what they owe: the activity log records the loan (amount, per-turn repayment, term) and the remaining obligation (turns left + per-turn amount) is surfaced in the HUD, so the debt burden is never hidden.
- The activity log records the loan (amount, per-turn repayment and term) when it is taken, and each repayment is recorded as an expense line.
- The HUD readout shows turns left and per-turn amount beside the coin and reputation readouts in both single-player and competitive layouts.
- The HUD readout is hidden when no loan is active or loans are disabled, and existing HUD layout anchors still pass.

# Persistence: loans and pending offer, save schema v3

Parent: MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG (Bank Loans). Depends on the loan model and bailout slices.

## Goal

A save taken mid-loan (or mid-offer) restores exactly: active loans keep their remaining
turns and repayment amounts, a pending bailout offer is still pending, and pre-loan saves
load unchanged.

## Context

- `serializeMainStreetState` / `deserializeMainStreetState`
  (`src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts`) with `MAIN_STREET_SAVE_SCHEMA_VERSION = 2` and a
  strict version check plus `migrateSerializedState` hook (`src/MainStreetSaveLoad.ts`).
  Bumping to 3 with defaults is the established path for new fields.
- The migration must default legacy saves to an empty `loans` list and no pending offer, so
  a pre-loan save continues with unchanged behaviour (parent AC9).
- Existing coverage: `tests/main-street/save-load.test.ts` and
  `tests/main-street/CalendarSaveLoad.test.ts` show the round-trip/migration test shape;
  the migration browser test (`tests/main-street/MainStreetMigration.browser.test.ts`)
  covers legacy browser saves.
- Campaign save data (`MAIN_STREET_CAMPAIGN_SCHEMA_VERSION`) is separate — do not bump it
  unless a field genuinely needs it.

## Desired change

1. Serialise `loans` (all fields needed to resume the schedule: principal, total,
   per-turn, turns remaining, term, ownerId) and `pendingLoanOffer` (owner, reason,
   options); omit or null them when empty so diffs stay small.
2. Bump `MAIN_STREET_SAVE_SCHEMA_VERSION` to 3, add a v2 → v3 migration defaulting to no
   loans and no pending offer, and accept v2 saves through it.
3. Restore defensively: unknown/invalid loan entries are dropped rather than crashing the
   load, and `turnsRemaining` is clamped to `termTurns`.
4. Tests: round-trip with an active loan (remaining turns and per-turn amount preserved),
   round-trip with a pending offer, v2 save loads with empty loans and unchanged behaviour,
   and a mid-loan save resumes with the correct remaining payments.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Active loans and a pending loan offer survive a save/load round-trip, and the save schema version is bumped to 3 with a migration.
- Pre-loan saves at schema version 2 load with no loans and unchanged behaviour, proven by a migration test.
- Save/load round-trip and v2 migration tests cover loans and the pending offer, including the remaining repayment schedule.

## Key Files:

- `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` — serialise/restore loans and the pending offer, migration
- `src/MainStreetSaveLoad.ts` — `MAIN_STREET_SAVE_SCHEMA_VERSION` bump and migration hook
- `src/MainStreetLoans.ts` — restore/validation helpers
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetLoanSaveLoad.test.ts` — new round-trip and migration tests
- `tests/main-street/save-load.test.ts` — existing round-trip precedent (extend if shared helpers change)

# Wire Bank Loan button into the Turn Summary dialog

Follow-up raised by the Bank Loans planning session (MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG), per producer
decision Q4: the Turn Summary dialog (MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41) has landed, so its deliberately
disabled **Bank Loan** affordance can now be wired to the loan feature.

## Problem statement

The Turn Summary dialog shows an always-disabled **[ Bank Loan ]** button and never calls
the `onBankLoanAction` seam reserved for the loans feature, so a mid-game player has no
entry point to credit at all — the loan engine only surfaces offers on bankruptcy. This item
turns the reserved affordance into a working mid-game loan entry point, with no new engine
rules.

## Users

- **Mid-game human player (single-player)** — "When the Turn Summary dialog is on screen
  and I am short of cash, I want to borrow from the configured loan menu so I can fund the
  next week's move, and I want to see the repayment schedule before I commit."
- **Cautious player** — "I want the button to tell me *why* it is unavailable (loans turned
  off, or I already owe money) instead of a generic 'coming soon' note."

Not a user of this slice: competitive seats (per-seat closing text, no summary dialog),
AI seats (bailout-only policy — no proactive loans).

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Enabled/disabled matrix.** The Bank Loan button is interactive only when
   `state.config.loansEnabled === true` **and** the acting (human) seat holds no active loan;
   in every other case it is rendered disabled (muted, `input` disabled) with a hint that
   explains the reason.
2. **Selector with schedule.** Pressing the enabled button opens the loan selector listing
   every configured `config.loanOptions` entry with its per-turn repayment and total
   repayment, plus a way to back out; backing out returns to the Turn Summary dialog with no
   state change.
3. **Confirm dispatches `takeLoan`.** Confirming an option dispatches the `takeLoan` command
   for the acting seat, credits the principal to that seat's wallet, records the active loan,
   and leaves `actionsRemaining` unchanged.
4. **No day advance.** Neither opening the selector nor confirming a loan advances the day or
   resumes the deferred closing; the day advances only on **[ Next Turn ]**, exactly once.
5. **Refreshed dialog.** After the loan is taken the Turn Summary dialog is re-rendered from
   the same `TurnResult` with the post-`takeLoan` state, so the new obligation is visible and
   the button is now disabled (one-active-loan rule) while **[ Next Turn ]** still works.
6. **Testing/validation.** Tests cover the enabled/disabled matrix (loans enabled + no loan,
   active loan, `loansEnabled: false`), the selector content, the `takeLoan` dispatch, the
   no-action-point rule, the cancel path, and that the day does not advance before
   **[ Next Turn ]**.
7. **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
   code comments (`showTurnSummaryDialog`, the gate, the button-construction site),
   `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` (the "[ Bank Loan ] is always disabled" paragraph), and the
   in-game help/loan documentation touched by MS-0MVPWSFDN000QJXB.
8. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — `showTurnSummaryDialog(summary, onNextTurn,
  onBankLoanAction?)` renders `[ Bank Loan ]` with `disableInteractive()`, colour
  `#6b6459`, and the hint *“Bank loans are not available yet — coming in a future update.”*;
  it explicitly does `void onBankLoanAction` so the seam can never fire. `BANK_LOAN_HINT` is
  duplicated in `tests/main-street/turn-summary-dialog.browser.test.ts`, whose AC4 asserts
  "always disabled, seam never invoked" — that test must be rewritten, not deleted.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — `showTurnSummaryDialog(summary, onNextTurn,
  onBankLoanAction?)` delegates to `msOverlayManager`; with no overlay manager (headless) it
  calls `onNextTurn()` immediately so the closing is never stranded.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — `shouldGateTurnSummary()` restricts the
  dialog to `requiresDeferredClosing` single-player closings (never replay, reduced motion,
  tutorial or competitive); `presentTurnSummaryGate()` builds the summary with
  `buildTurnSummary(s.state, result)` and calls
  `s.showTurnSummaryDialog(summary, onNextTurn)` — the third argument is not passed today.
- Overlays already read live state (`s.state.config` in `MainStreetOverlayContent`), so
  `loansEnabled` needs no new plumbing into the scene.
- `buildTurnSummary()` is Phaser-free and read-only, so re-rendering after a loan only needs
  the same `state` + `result` pair re-run.
- **The loan engine does not exist yet.** `src/MainStreetLoans.ts`, `config.loansEnabled`,
  `config.loanOptions`, the `takeLoan` command and `src/scenes/MainStreetLoanOverlay.ts` are
  all still unimplemented: the Bank Loans epic MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG sits at
  `intake_complete`, its slices are `blocked` (only the headless determinism baseline,
  MS-0MVPWS45N008PR0X, is in flight). This item is the epic's only out-of-epic follow-up and
  must land *after* the model, `takeLoan`, and overlay-UI slices.
- Save schema v3 (loans + pending offer) is delivered by the epic; this slice must not touch
  serialisation.

## Desired change

1. **Carry a loans descriptor into the dialog.** Extend the gate's call so the dialog receives
   one small Phaser-free descriptor rather than reaching into scene state ad hoc — predicted
   shape `{ enabled: boolean; activeLoan: { perTurnRepayment, turnsRemaining } | null;
   options: LoanOption[] }` built in `presentTurnSummaryGate()` from `s.state.config` and the
   acting seat. Keeps the overlay presentation-only and the descriptor unit-testable.
   (Implementation may instead read `s.state` directly if the epic's helpers make that
   cleaner — the ACs do not care which; see Assumptions.)
2. **Enable the affordance** when `enabled && activeLoan === null`, wiring `pointerdown` to
   the `onBankLoanAction` seam; keep the button disabled otherwise with a reason-specific
   hint (loans disabled vs. already owing — see open question Q3).
3. **Loan selector** presented on press: reuse the epic's `MainStreetLoanOverlay` option rows
   (per-turn + total repayment). The epic builds it for a *pending offer* driven by
   `state.pendingLoanOffer`; this slice needs a non-bailout mode (no pending offer, options
   from `config.loanOptions`, Cancel/back instead of Decline). Reusing the row renderer, not
   duplicating it, is the requirement; a small `mode` parameter is expected.
4. **Confirm = dispatch.** Confirming dispatches the `takeLoan` command through the existing
   command surface (`src/MainStreetCommands.ts`), never mutating state inline.
5. **Refresh in place** after a successful take: rebuild the summary from the same
   `TurnResult` and re-render the dialog (dismiss the old overlay objects first so
   `s.overlayObjects` stays consistent), leaving `[ Next Turn ]` as the only way to resume
   `advanceTurn`.
6. **Tests** in a new `tests/main-street/turn-summary-bank-loan.browser.test.ts` (browser
   overlay, mirroring `turn-summary-dialog.browser.test.ts` helpers) plus the rewrite of the
   dialog suite's AC4 case.

## Constraints

- **Presentation wiring only** — no new engine rules, no changes to the loan model, repayment
  maths or one-active-loan validation; those belong to MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG.
- **No action point cost** and **no day advance** — taking a loan from the dialog must leave
  `actionsRemaining` untouched and must not resume the deferred closing.
- **Single-player deferred path only** — the dialog itself is gated to that path; competitive
  per-seat closing and the tutorial/reduced-motion/replay paths are unchanged.
- **Overlay conventions** (`core` UI best practices): `createOverlayBackground` +
  `createOverlayButton`, all elements parented into `s.hudContainer` and pushed to
  `s.overlayObjects`, depths 199/200/201, instant appearance (reduced-motion safe), SFX via
  `safePlaySound`.
- **Blocked-by sequencing** — depends on MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG (dependency edge already
  recorded): specifically the loan model/config slice (MS-0MVPWS5JB007YSHB), the `takeLoan`
  command slice (MS-0MVPWS6WB008WP79) and the overlay-UI slice (MS-0MVPWSBLG006YMBA).

## Assumptions

- **A1 First repayment falls on the next turn's closing.** The closing sequence (and its
  ledger) has already run when the dialog is presented, so a loan taken at the dialog must not
  charge a repayment against the turn being summarised. Recorded as OPEN QUESTION Q1 for
  producer confirmation.
- **A2 Proactive loans are allowed at any coin balance** — the button is not gated on
  affordability or negative coins (the goal is mid-game credit, not a second bailout path).
- **A3 The selector's rows come from `config.loanOptions`**, so a re-balanced menu needs no UI
  change, and the dialog is unavailable (button disabled) when the menu is empty.
- **A4 `takeLoan` rejection is surfaced, not swallowed** — if the engine refuses (e.g. a race
  into an active loan), the dialog shows the engine's reason and stays open rather than
  silently closing.
- **A5 Headless safety is untouched** — with no overlay manager the scene still calls
  `onNextTurn()`; the new descriptor must remain optional so existing call sites compile.

## Risks & mitigations

- **Sequencing risk (highest):** the epic is not implemented; starting this slice early would
  mean inventing engine helpers (scope creep). Mitigation: keep the item dependency-blocked
  until the three prerequisites are `completed`.
- **Duplicated overlay logic:** copy-pasting the bailout overlay instead of parameterising it
  would leave two loan selectors to maintain. Mitigation: AC2/desired-change 3 require reusing
  the epic's row renderer.
- **Stale dialog content:** re-rendering from a mutated `state` but a stale `TurnResult` can
  show a mismatch. Mitigation: rebuild via `buildTurnSummary(state, result)` with the same
  `result` object (the ledger is presentation data, not recomputed).
- **Overlay object leak:** dismissing and re-rendering must reset `s.overlayObjects` the same
  way `dismissOverlay` does, or duplicated buttons accumulate in `hudContainer`. Mitigation:
  explicit test asserting a single `[ Next Turn ]`/`[ Bank Loan ]` pair after a refresh.
- **Test drift:** `turn-summary-dialog.browser.test.ts` AC4 encodes "always disabled"; leaving
  it untouched makes the suite self-contradictory. Mitigation: rewrite that case in the same
  commit.
- **Scope creep:** competitive-mode parity (MS-0MVO1SFCM000ZLBI), AI proactive loans, multiple
  loans, loan repayment UI polish — record as linked work items, do not fold in.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — enable/disable `[ Bank Loan ]`, wire the seam,
  render the reason-specific hint and refresh the dialog after a take.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — build and pass the loans descriptor in
  `presentTurnSummaryGate()`; keep `shouldGateTurnSummary()` unchanged.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — pass the descriptor through the delegation method.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetLoanOverlay.ts` — reuse the epic's option rows in a non-bailout
  (mid-game select) mode.
- `src/MainStreetLoans.ts` — consume `activeLoanFor` / option-table helpers (read-only use).
- `src/MainStreetCommands.ts` — `takeLoan` command dispatch and the no-AP assertion.
- `tests/main-street/turn-summary-bank-loan.browser.test.ts` — **new.** Wiring tests.
- `tests/main-street/turn-summary-dialog.browser.test.ts` — rewrite the "seam never invoked"
  case.
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` — update the "always disabled" Turn Summary paragraph.

## Out of scope / non-goals

- Competitive-mode summary dialog and any competitive loan entry point
  (MS-0MVO1SFCM000ZLBI).
- Engine rules: repayment timing, bailout offer loop, AI policy, persistence — owned by
  MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG.
- HUD obligation readout (MS-0MVPWSCRD004A6Z4) and the loans help/documentation slice
  (MS-0MVPWSFDN000QJXB); this item only edits the one doc paragraph it invalidates.

## Related work

- **MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG** (Bank Loans, epic, `intake_complete`) — the engine this slice wires
  into; dependency edge recorded.
- **MS-0MVPWS5JB007YSHB** (Loan model, config and repayment maths), **MS-0MVPWS6WB008WP79**
  (`takeLoan` command and one-active-loan rule), **MS-0MVPWSBLG006YMBA** (Bailout overlay UI
  and deferred closing resume) — prerequisites.
- **MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41** (End of Turn summary, completed) — parent of the dialog; its AC
  anticipated the Bank Loan button.
- **MS-0MVP46AMO002SZUT** (Overlay: turn summary dialog + browser test, completed) — created
  the disabled affordance and its `onBankLoanAction` seam.
- **MS-0MVP46Q8X003419R** (deferred closing gate, completed) — the gate that presents the
  dialog; see `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` § "Turn Summary dialog and the closing gate".
- **MS-0MVO1SFCM000ZLBI** (End of Turn summary dialog for competitive mode, open) — the other
  mode's dialog; explicitly not covered here.
- Repo: `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts`,
  `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts`, `tests/main-street/turn-summary-dialog.browser.test.ts`,
  `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md`.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (repayment timing): "A loan taken from the Turn Summary dialog — when does the first
  repayment hit? (A) at the next turn's closing, since this turn's closing and ledger have
  already run [recommended]; (B) immediately when the deferred closing resumes, so the turn
  just summarised carries it; (C) other." — **OPEN QUESTION.** No answer yet; the item is
  blocked by the epic anyway. Draft assumes **A** (see Assumption A1). Source: raised in the
  intake session 2026-10-27, no interactive producer available (auto-dispatched downtime run).
- Q2 (mode scope): "Should the enabled button also cover any non-single-player summary
  surface? (A) no — single-player deferred path only; competitive parity stays with
  MS-0MVO1SFCM000ZLBI [recommended]; (B) cover competitive too." — **OPEN QUESTION**, draft
  assumes **A** (already consistent with `shouldGateTurnSummary`).
- Q3 (disabled hint wording): "When the seat already holds an active loan, what should the
  disabled hint say? (A) show the outstanding obligation, e.g. *'Active loan: 110 coins/week,
  4 weeks left.'* [recommended]; (B) a generic *'You already have an active loan.'*; (C) keep
  the current generic text." — **OPEN QUESTION**, draft assumes **A**.
- Q4 (proactive eligibility): "Is the button available at any balance, or only when the seat
  cannot cover its costs?" — answered from the seed goal (mid-game credit use case): **any
  balance**, recorded as Assumption A2. Source: work-item description "As a mid-game player …
  I can click [ Bank Loan ]".
- Q5 (selector reuse): "Does the epic's bailout overlay support a non-bailout option list?" —
  research: `src/scenes/MainStreetLoanOverlay.ts` does not exist yet; the epic's Key Files
  predict it as the pending-offer overlay. Draft therefore requires a reuse with a mode
  parameter rather than a copy (Risks: duplicated overlay logic). Source: `wl show
  MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG --json`, `ls src/scenes/`.
- Q6 (dependency): "Is the loan engine available to wire against?" — research: no — `grep -ri
  loan src` returns only the dialog's placeholder comments; the epic is at `intake_complete`
  with its slices `blocked`. Recorded as a hard prerequisite. Source: repo grep, `wl search
  loan --json`.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MVP46AMO002SZUT** – Overlay: turn summary dialog + browser test (completed)
- **MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41** – End of Turn summary. When all animations for the End of Turn phase have completed we should pop up a dialog with details of the current state of the game. # of businesses owned by each player, income and expenses for that turn, one-off income/expenses (from events etc.) and any other information that would be useful and informative. The dialog will have a "next turn" button and a "Bank Loan" button which will allow them to take out a loan (a feature not yet implemented, see work item) (completed)
- **MS-0MVO1SFCM000ZLBI** – End of Turn summary dialog for competitive mode (open)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` — matched: 0mvl6dzi0000f6cg, 0mvl6hmdp004wi41, action, active, advance (+104 more)
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: acceptance, action, active, advance, already (+102 more)
- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: acceptance, acting, action, active, advance (+87 more)

# Reproduce pre-change soak-load failure baseline

## Headline

Reproduce the `turn to advance after end-of-turn presentation` wait failure on the pre-change baseline (dev tip before any deferral-helper extraction) at ≥ `nproc` (16) burners, recording the before-table as the evidence anchor for MS-0MVMKEU2000639TG. Runs through `/skill:test --type soak-load` (the policy-compliant harness) only — no ad-hoc vitest loops.

## Summary

The soak evidence on MS-0MVLINY2Q004V33L shows the gate fails exactly one wait at load ≥ ≈31 (≈2× oversubscription). This child re-runs that failing profile against the unmodified baseline in the item's worktree to (a) confirm the failure reproduces at the current dev tip (git state, not just the 2026-10-24 record), and (b) produce the before-table the parent AC requires. If the host cannot reach ambient load ≈31 with 16 burners, the achieved profile is recorded honestly instead of being re-labelled.

**Key Files:**

## Summary

Implements the parent's decision C: the helper computes its deadline from `Date.now()`, re-polls with `window.setTimeout` (not the scene clock), forces completion after `INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` of wall time, enforces the cap even when the page is not painting (Q2 = 1), degrades to immediate continuation where no clock/timer exists, and exposes its clock/timer for deterministic unit driving. No deferral site is adopted here (adoption is the next child, keeping the change reviewable); production pacing constants are untouched.

# Transient feedback toasts: readable hold, animate/pause/fade, always on top

**Headline:** Main Street's transient feedback toast (the channel that explains an illegal move, e.g. "Not enough coins to place Bakery") is currently a single 1.1 s pop that starts fading immediately and renders at depth 0, inside the hand band — so it cannot be read and is covered by hand cards. Make it a proper toast: fade/pop in, hold fully opaque for 0.5 s per word, fade out, render above every other scene element, and clear the hand band.

## Problem statement

When a move is refused, the player gets an explanation through `flashError()` → `flashFeedback()` (`src/scenes/MainStreetFeedback.ts`). The message is created by `popTextOrIcon` with a 1.1 s total lifetime, a fade that begins on the first frame, depth 0, and an anchor at `handY − 20` — which is inside the hand-card row (cards are centred on `handY`, so the top of the cards is `handY − handCardH/2`). The result is text that is too fast to read and is covered by the hand and higher-depth HUD/overlay layers.

## Users

- **Player (primary):** "When I make an illegal move, I want to read *why* it was refused without racing the fade or the hand, so I can correct my move instead of guessing."
- **Reduced-motion player:** "I still need the same explanation held for the same readable time, without animation."
- **QA/designer:** "I want the toast's timing and layer to be deterministic and assertable, so a regression is caught by the suite rather than by playing the game."
- **Developer:** "I want one place that owns toast presentation so the feedback channel stays consistent as more messages move into it."

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Word-based readable hold.** A pure helper (e.g. `feedbackHoldMs(text)`) derives the fully-opaque hold from the message's whitespace-delimited word count: `words × 500 ms` (minimum one word's 500 ms). The toast stays at alpha 1 for exactly that hold between fade-in and fade-out; a 5-word refusal is readable for 2.5 s, not 1.1 s total. Unit tests cover 1, 5 and 10-word messages and empty text.
- [ ] **AC2 — Animate → pause → fade.** Normal presentation runs fade/scale-in (~160 ms), the AC1 fully-opaque pause, then fade-out (~300 ms) before destruction; total lifetime is `fadeIn + hold + fadeOut`. No fade or motion occurs during the pause. Under reduced motion the toast is static at alpha 1 for the same AC1 hold and is then destroyed — no tweens, never dropped. Unit tests assert the sequence, that alpha stays 1 through the hold, and that reduced motion creates no tween.
- [ ] **AC3 — Always above, clear of the hand.** Both the animated and reduced-motion toasts render at a named depth above every Main Street layer (hand cards 0…n, hand panel −100, action row 100, overlays 200–201, stats 900–950, HUD 1000, stats button 1100), e.g. `FEEDBACK_TOAST_DEPTH = 3000`. The anchor is lifted clear of the hand-card band (`handY − handCardH/2 − margin`) using layout values, with a safe fallback when metrics are missing. Tests assert the applied depth and anchor with the real layout shape.
- [ ] **AC4 — One readable toast, wrapped.** Only one feedback toast is live per scene: a new message destroys the previous toast, cancels its hold/dismiss timers and starts fresh (no stacked duplicates at the same anchor). Long messages word-wrap within the viewport (max width derived from `gameW`) and carry a dark stroke so they stay legible over any background. Tests cover replacement/cancellation and wrap-width selection.
- [ ] **AC5 — Existing feedback contract unchanged.** Message taxonomy (error/confirmation surfaced; guidance/progress dropped), `scene.lastFeedback` / `scene.feedbackHistory`, Activity Log behaviour and the `flashError`/`flashConfirmation` API remain unchanged; the toast is never interactive and never intercepts pointer input. Existing feedback/illegal-afford tests stay green (anchor expectations updated only for the deliberate lift).
- [ ] **AC6 — All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README where relevant, and the VitePress pages under `docs/` (in particular `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` § *Transient pop-text feedback channel*).
- [ ] **AC7 — Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **In-repo only.** Implement in `src/scenes/` (Main Street). Do **not** edit the engine-owned `core/` submodule or bump the engine pin; the engine's `illegalMoveToast` is a separate component and is not composed by Main Street at this pin.
- **Reduced motion is mandatory.** The in-game setting / `prefers-reduced-motion` path must remain animation-free while preserving the same hold time.
- **No input capture.** The toast is presentation-only; do not make it interactive.
- **Deterministic and testable.** Drive timing through Phaser time/tweens (or an injected clock in tests), never fixed real-time sleeps.
- **Base layout is 1280×720 but expands.** Use layout values (`handY`, `handCardH`, `gameW`, `logX`) rather than new hard-coded pixel positions.
- **Scope is feedback toasts.** Animation-only `popTextOrIcon` effects (income counters, level-up, card-transfer VFX) keep their current short pop; word-based dwell would stall their animation sequences.
- CHANGELOG.md is excluded (managed by the ship release pipeline). Do not add CI/CD pipeline tests.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/MainStreetFeedback.ts`:
  - `flashFeedback()` records `scene.lastFeedback` / `feedbackHistory`, then uses `duration = options.duration ?? 1100`.
  - Normal path calls `popTextOrIcon({ scene, x, y, label, duration: 1100, riseY: 20, scale: 1.1, reducedMotion: false })`.
  - Reduced-motion path creates `scene.add.text(...).setOrigin(0.5).setDepth(900)` and destroys it after `duration`.
  - `feedbackAnchor(layout)` returns `{ x: logX / 2, y: handY − 20 }`.
- `popTextOrIcon` (`@ui/popTextOrIcon`, engine-owned) runs one tween for the whole duration: `y −20`, `alpha → 0`, `scale 1.1`. There is no pause, and the text has no explicit depth (defaults to 0) or wrap width.
- Depth landscape: hand cards use `depth = index` (0…n), hand panel `−100`, action row `100`, overlays `200–201`, stats `900–950`, HUD `1000`, stats button `1100`. A depth-0 toast therefore sits under hand cards and every HUD/overlay layer.
- Tests: `tests/main-street/feedback-pop-text.test.ts` mocks `popTextOrIcon` and asserts anchor `{ x: 410, y: 600 }` for `{ logX: 820, handY: 620 }`, plus the reduced-motion static path. `tests/main-street/illegal-afford-feedback.test.ts` asserts `scene.lastFeedback` text for refusals.
- Docs: `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` documents the current 1100 ms `popTextOrIcon` presentation.

## Desired change

1. **Pure timing helper:** `feedbackHoldMs(text: string): number` → `max(1, wordCount) × 500` ms; empty/whitespace text returns 0 (no toast). Export it for tests.
2. **Toast presentation in `MainStreetFeedback`:** create the text at the anchor with `FONT_FAMILY` and the existing 18 px bold white style, origin 0.5, `setDepth(FEEDBACK_TOAST_DEPTH)`, `setWordWrapWidth(min(FEEDBACK_TOAST_MAX_WIDTH, gameW − 40))`, dark stroke, alpha 0/scale 0.9. Fade/scale in over `FEEDBACK_TOAST_FADE_IN_MS`, hold for `feedbackHoldMs(text)`, fade out over `FEEDBACK_TOAST_FADE_OUT_MS`, then destroy. Reduced motion: alpha 1, no tweens, destroy after the hold.
3. **Replacement:** keep at most one toast per scene (module `WeakMap` or a scene field); on a new message, cancel the previous hold timer/tweens and destroy the previous text before showing the new one. Bind scene shutdown/destroy cleanup so no timer or text leaks.
4. **Anchor:** `feedbackAnchor` gains the hand-card height (optional for backward compatibility) and returns `y = handY − handCardH/2 − FEEDBACK_TOAST_MARGIN_PX`; keep the current `logX / 2` horizontal centring and the safe fallback when layout metrics are missing.
5. **Constants:** add `FEEDBACK_TOAST_DEPTH`, `FEEDBACK_TOAST_FADE_IN_MS`, `FEEDBACK_TOAST_FADE_OUT_MS`, `FEEDBACK_WORD_HOLD_MS = 500`, `FEEDBACK_TOAST_MARGIN_PX`, `FEEDBACK_TOAST_MAX_WIDTH` to `src/scenes/MainStreetConstants.ts` (or a small local block if that file is not the right home).
6. **Tests:** rework `tests/main-street/feedback-pop-text.test.ts` to assert `feedbackHoldMs`, the fade→hold→fade sequence with a fake scene, alpha 1 during the hold, depth/wrap/anchor, replacement/cancellation, reduced motion with no tweens, and unchanged classification/history. Keep `illegal-afford-feedback.test.ts` green.
7. **Docs:** update `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` § *Transient pop-text feedback channel* (hold formula, sequence, depth, anchor, replacement, reduced motion).

**Order of work (test-first):** write the new timing/presentation tests against the agreed contract, then the helper and constants, then the presentation/replacement and anchor lift, then the docs.

**Key Files:**

- `src/scenes/MainStreetFeedback.ts` — New helper, toast presentation/replacement, anchor lift, reduced-motion path.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetConstants.ts` — New toast depth, fade/hold/margin/wrap constants if not kept local to the feedback module.
- `tests/main-street/feedback-pop-text.test.ts` — Reworked timing, depth, anchor, replacement and reduced-motion tests.
- `tests/main-street/illegal-afford-feedback.test.ts` — Regression: illegal-move reasons still surface through `lastFeedback`.
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` — Update the transient feedback channel presentation contract.

## Related work

- **MS-0MVPWQK3U003DIR6** (completed, `in_review`) — *[Impl] Remove instruction line and route feedback to pop text*: introduced `MainStreetFeedback`, `feedbackAnchor`, `lastFeedback`/`feedbackHistory`, and the 1100 ms `popTextOrIcon` presentation this item replaces.
- **MS-0MVKTB6WS000VLWK** (completed, `in_review`) — *UI simplification when roads are visible*: parent decision that errors/confirmations are surfaced as transient pop text and guidance/progress are dropped (Q4a). This item keeps that taxonomy.
- **CG-0MVPXFHBZ004LGEB** (engine, completed) — *Core illegal-move routine: explain a rejected move with a reason toast*: adds an engine-side `illegalMoveToast` (dwell 2500 ms, depth 1900, y 520). It is **not** composed by Main Street at the pinned engine `0409c1eb`, and `playIllegalFeedback()` does not pass a `reason`; Main Street's visible illegal-move explanation is the `flashError` toast. If the producer intended that engine toast instead, this item must be re-scoped to `~/projects/Tableau-Card-Engine` plus a Main Street re-pin.
- **MS-0MVQO6N34007DHP8** (critical) — *Bumping the engine pin to core dev tip breaks the unit suite (`phaser window is not defined`)*: relevant only if scope is later widened to the engine toast; it does not block the in-repo feedback toast fix.
- **Docs:** `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` § *Transient pop-text feedback channel*; `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (illegal feedback description).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — observed toast is the Main Street feedback channel.** At the pinned engine `0409c1eb`, `shakeIllegalMove` has no `reason` toast and `playIllegalFeedback` passes no reason, so the illegal-move reason the player sees is `flashError` → `flashFeedback` (1100 ms, depth 0, inside the hand band). This exactly matches the report. Research: `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerDragDrop.ts:62`, `src/scenes/MainStreetFeedback.ts:88`, `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerUtils.ts:20-64`, `core` gitlink `0409c1eb`.
- **Assumption — scope is feedback toasts only.** `popTextOrIcon` is also used directly for short animation VFX (income `+€`, level-up, card transfer). Those are markers, not explanations; applying a word-based hold would stall animation sequences and is out of scope.
- **Risk — scope creep into the engine toast.** The engine's shared `illegalMoveToast` has the same readability problem (fixed 2500 ms dwell, y 520, depth 1900). It is deliberately not bundled here; record it as a separate engine item and a re-pin if the producer wants it.
- **Risk — long messages linger.** A 20-word reason holds for 10 s. This is the producer's explicit 0.5 s/word rule; the toast is non-interactive and can be replaced by the next message, so it does not block play. No cap is added unless the producer asks for one.
- **Risk — depth above overlays.** `FEEDBACK_TOAST_DEPTH = 3000` puts the toast above the stats/help overlays and the HUD. A toast raised while a modal is open will sit over the modal for its bounded lifetime; replacement and auto-dismiss keep that window short. The producer explicitly asked for "above all other elements".
- **Risk — regression in tests pinned to the old anchor.** `feedback-pop-text.test.ts` asserts `y: 600`; the deliberate lift changes that to `handY − handCardH/2 − margin`. Update the assertions with the new contract, do not weaken them.
- **Risk — leaked timers/tweens.** Replacement and scene shutdown must cancel pending hold/fade timers and destroy the text; tests use fake time to prove no callbacks fire after replacement.
- **Assumption — no background panel.** Legibility is achieved with a dark stroke over the text rather than a filled chip; the producer asked for animate/pause/fade/on-top, not a panel. A chip can be added later if the stroke is not enough.
- **Assumption — `duration` option.** No call site passes `FeedbackOptions.duration`; its role is replaced by the word-based hold. To avoid a silent breaking change, keep an optional explicit hold override (renamed `holdMs`) for tests/back-compat and default it to `feedbackHoldMs(text)`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No producer interview was required: the seed context (too fast, animate/pause/fade, 0.5 s per word, above all elements) plus repository investigation resolved the scope and contract. Each resolution is recorded for producer review.

- Q: "Which toast is the report about — Main Street's feedback pop text or the engine's `illegalMoveToast`?" — Answer (agent, repository investigation): **Main Street's feedback pop text**. Research: the pinned engine is `0409c1eb`, before the engine reason-toast commit `34e0ab6d`; `playIllegalFeedback()` calls `shakeIllegalMove` without a `reason`, so no engine toast is rendered in Main Street. The illegal-move reason is surfaced by `flashError()` (`MainStreetTurnControllerDragDrop.ts:62`) through `flashFeedback` → `popTextOrIcon` at 1100 ms, depth 0, anchor `handY − 20` (inside the hand band). Source: `git -C core log --all -- src/ui/illegalMoveToast.ts`, `src/scenes/MainStreetFeedback.ts`, `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerUtils.ts`.
- Q: "Does 'toasts' include every `popTextOrIcon` call, e.g. income and level-up numbers?" — Answer (agent): **No — feedback toasts only** (`flashFeedback`/`flashError`/`flashConfirmation`). Research: direct `popTextOrIcon` calls are animation VFX with short, self-explanatory labels and are sequenced with board animations; a word-based hold would stall them. Source: `grep -rn popTextOrIcon src/scenes`, `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` § *Event Feedback Animations*.
- Q: "What exactly should 'animate, pause, fade' mean, and how is the 0.5 s/word pause applied?" — Answer (agent): **fade/scale-in ~160 ms → fully opaque hold of `words × 500 ms` → fade-out ~300 ms**; total lifetime is the sum. Reduced motion skips the tweens but keeps the same hold. Source: producer's seed description; implemented contract in AC1/AC2.
- Q: "What does 'above all other elements' mean for layer depth?" — Answer (agent): **a named depth above every Main Street layer** (`FEEDBACK_TOAST_DEPTH = 3000`, above hand cards 0…n, hand panel −100, action 100, overlays 200–201, stats 900–950, HUD 1000, stats button 1100), plus an anchor lifted clear of the hand-card band. Source: `grep -rn setDepth src/scenes core/src/ui/HandView.ts`, `MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` hand-panel geometry.
- Q: "Should a new message stack with the previous toast or replace it?" — Answer (agent): **replace**. Research: repeated refusals currently create multiple overlapping `popTextOrIcon` texts at the same anchor; one live toast is the readable and testable contract. Source: `MainStreetFeedback.flashFeedback` current create-per-call behaviour; engine `illegalMoveToast` precedent (single live toast per scene).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MVKTB6WS000VLWK** – UI simplification when roads are visible (completed)
- **MS-0MUMP96XH002SJ89** – Named storylines, outcome feedback & continuity indicator (completed)
- **MS-0MVPWQO3B008B574** – [Docs] Document opaque panels, hand anchor and hint removal (completed)

- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` — matched: 0mvpwqk3u003dir6, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4 (+394 more)
