# Third stats column with five graphs

Parent: MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV — End of game stats (phase 3, main deliverable).

## Goal (user story)

As a Main Street player at game over, I want a third column of graphs showing
my profit, cash, businesses, staff and reputation turn by turn, plus a link
from the Summary to that detail, so I can see what worked and what did not.

## Scope

- **In:** third column composition of five graphs, panel/column geometry
  rebalance to fit 1280×720, the Summary → stats affordance, overlay
  conventions.
- **Out:** competitive-mode series assertions and both-mode fit verification
  (competitive child), prose docs (docs child), additional stats or chart types
  (producer Q4 = none; raise as separate items).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Graphs.** The Game Over overlay renders a **third column** containing the
   five end-of-game graphs.
2. **Graph details.** The column is headed `Stats`, sits to the right of
   `Summary`, and contains, in order: **profit per turn**, **cash at end of
   turn**, **businesses at end of turn**, **staff at end of turn** and
   **reputation at end of turn**, each chart fed from
   `buildGameOverStatSeries(state)` with a visible axis/legend label. An overlay
   unit test (chart module mocked) asserts five chart specs with the expected
   series and titles.
3. **Summary cash line + link.** The Summary column shows the final cash and
   links the stats column.
4. **Link detail.** The affordance is a `[ View detailed stats ]` control that
   focuses the stats column without animation (static focus frame and/or depth
   raise), is keyboard-activatable via `setInteractive`, reads no mutable state,
   and leaves `state` unchanged when activated (unit test).
5. **Layout fits 1280×720.** `panelW` / `colW` / `colGap` / `panelH` are
   recomputed so three columns fit inside the 1280×720 viewport with no
   horizontal or vertical overflow (`panelH ≤ gameH − 2 × margin`, box inside
   the viewport) and no text clipping; the existing Summary content (score
   breakdown, challenge details, tier/campaign, difficulty, buttons) is
   retained; an overlay unit test asserts the geometry for a rich history
   (≥ 12 turns) and an empty history.
6. **Overlay conventions.** The new UI honours the established overlay
   conventions: `hudContainer` parenting, depths 199/200/201 and
   `overlayObjects`.
7. **Conventions detail.** Content is created only after the existing
   `scene.replayMode` early return; no tweens, rAF or other animation is added
   by the new column (reduced-motion safe); the overlay remains a read-only
   view of committed state.
8. **Tests.** Unit coverage for the composition and geometry (mocked chart
   module) plus a browser test asserting the three column headers and five
   chart canvases render in a real scene at 1280×720.

## Minimal implementation

1. `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts` — any small series/label helpers
   the column needs (still Phaser-free).
2. `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — three-column layout maths
   (`panelW`/`colW`/`colGap`/`panelH`/`statsX`), `Stats` header, five chart
   placements, Summary cash line + `[ View detailed stats ]` affordance.
3. `src/scenes/MainStreetStatsChart.ts` — chart spec type used by the column.
4. Tests: extend `tests/main-street/game-over-overlay.test.ts`; add
   `tests/main-street/game-over-stats-column.browser.test.ts`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — third column, layout, affordance.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts` — series/label helpers.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetStatsChart.ts` — chart spec + creation.
- `tests/main-street/game-over-overlay.test.ts` — composition/geometry unit
  assertions.
- `tests/main-street/game-over-stats-column.browser.test.ts` — **new** browser
  fit/visibility assertions.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the chart-library spike (wrapper + lazy load) and the
capture/series-model child. Blocks the competitive and docs children.

## Deliverables

Third column with five graphs, Summary link, layout rebalance, unit + browser
tests.

## Risks

- Three columns at 1280×720 is tight; five stacked charts may need compact
  chart heights — mitigated by the geometry assertion and a ≤ 12-turn rich
  fixture.
- The DOM chart layer must sit above the Phaser overlay box (depth 200) but
  below the buttons — verify pointer events are unaffected.

# Competitive-mode stats and both-mode fit

Parent: MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV — End of game stats (phase 4).

## Goal (user story)

As a competitive Main Street player, I want the same end-of-game graphs for my
own seat so a loss against the AI can be diagnosed, and I want the overlay to
fit the viewport in both game modes.

## Scope

- **In:** competitive-series scope, both-mode rendering/fit verification,
  replay/headless guard verification, reduced-motion confirmation.
- **Out:** per-seat multi-series graphs (only if the producer overrides the
  recorded working assumption — that would be a separate item), docs prose.

## Working assumption (plan Open Question)

Competitive mode plots the **human seat's** trajectory only (see the parent's
Appendix "OPEN QUESTION (competitive-mode series scope)"). This child asserts
and documents that assumption; it must not expand to per-seat series without
producer confirmation.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Competitive series.** With a competitive fixture (`players[]` populated),
   the rendered series equal the recorded `turnStatsHistory` for the human
   seat's closing values, and no AI seat's wallet leaks into the series (unit
   test asserting series points against a hand-built competitive history).
2. **Human-seat recording.** The competitive closing path records one history
   entry per turn from the seat-scoped closing wallet (`findHumanSeatId`
   semantics), never one entry per AI seat; a unit test drives a scripted
   competitive turn and asserts exactly one entry with the human seat's coins.
3. **Both modes and layout.** The overlay works in single-player and
   competitive modes and fits the 1280×720 layout.
4. **Both-mode render detail.** Browser tests assert the `Stats` column header,
   five chart canvases and the `Cash at end of turn` line render in
   **single-player** and **competitive** states, and that the panel stays
   inside 1280×720 with no clipping or vertical overflow in both.
5. **Replay/headless guard.** In `scene.replayMode` the overlay creates no
   chart canvas and no DOM node (unit test with a mocked scene asserting zero
   chart constructions), and headless Monte-Carlo/engine runs are unaffected
   (changed-scope tests green).
6. **Static, no animation.** No tweens or rAF are added by this child; the
   overlay is static so reduced-motion users see the same content.
7. **Scope discipline.** Any competitive-scope gap beyond the working
   assumption is recorded as an Open Question comment on the parent rather than
   implemented here.

## Minimal implementation

1. `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts` — seat-aware series selection
   (human seat) if the model needs the seat id.
2. `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — ensure the third column reads the
   same model in both modes; no separate competitive layout branch beyond what
   already exists.
3. Tests: competitive fixture in the unit suite; both-mode browser assertions;
   replay-mode no-DOM assertion.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts` — seat-aware series.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — both-mode column wiring.
- `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts` — record once per turn on the
  competitive closing tail (if not already covered by the shared tail).
- `tests/main-street/competitive-game-over-stats.test.ts` — **new** competitive
  series/recording tests.
- `tests/main-street/game-over-stats-column.browser.test.ts` — extended
  both-mode fit assertions.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the third-stats-column child. Blocks the docs and acceptance
children.

## Deliverables

Competitive series + recording tests, both-mode browser fit assertions,
replay/headless guard test, scope note.

## Risks

- Competitive closing may run per seat in some paths, producing duplicate
  entries for one turn — mitigated by the `turn`-keyed guard and AC2's test.
- Human-seat identification in a headless AI-only run — assert the fallback
  (first seat) is documented and tested.

# Document end-of-game stats

Parent: MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV — End of game stats (phase 5).

## Goal (user story)

As a designer or developer, I want the per-turn history and the end-of-game
stats column documented in the project docs, so balance analysis and future UI
work do not have to reverse-engineer the code.

## Scope

- **In:** markdown docs for the per-turn history and the third Game Over column,
  README/overlay README updates where features are enumerated, code-comment
  consistency pass, docs build.
- **Out:** `CHANGELOG.md` (managed by the ship pipeline); behaviour changes.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
   changes: mechanics docs, UX docs and README.
2. **Mechanics docs.** `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` documents
   `turnStatsHistory`: field shape, when a snapshot is recorded (every closed
   turn on the legacy, deferred and competitive paths), the `profit`
   definition reusing the `weekStartCoins` day-start snapshot, and persistence
   with the legacy empty-history fallback — cross-referenced from the existing
   Activity Log per-turn-net section.
3. **UX docs.** `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` documents the third Game Over
   column: the five graphs, the Summary `Cash at end of turn` line and
   `[ View detailed stats ]` affordance, the three-column 1280×720 layout
   budget, and the overlay conventions honoured (Phaser-free model,
   `hudContainer` parenting, depths 199/200/201, `overlayObjects`, replay
   early return, static/no-animation reduced-motion behaviour).
4. **Feature lists.** `README.md` and `src/scenes/README.md` mention the
   end-of-game stats column where the Game Over overlay / features are
   enumerated.
5. **Code comments.** JSDoc on `TurnStatSnapshot`, `recordTurnStats`,
   `buildGameOverStatSeries` and `MainStreetStatsChart` matches the documented
   behaviour, with no stale "two-column" wording left in touched files.
6. **Docs build.** `npm run docs:build` succeeds with the new content.

## Minimal implementation

1. Update `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (per-turn history section +
   cross-reference).
2. Update `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` (end-of-game stats column section).
3. Update `README.md` and `src/scenes/README.md` feature text.
4. Comment consistency pass over the touched source files.
5. Run `npm run docs:build`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — per-turn history.
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` — stats column + conventions.
- `README.md` — feature list.
- `src/scenes/README.md` — overlay module list.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts`, `src/scenes/MainStreetStatsChart.ts`,
  `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — JSDoc consistency.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the third-stats-column and competitive-mode children (documents the
shipped behaviour). Blocks the acceptance-verification child.

## Deliverables

Updated markdown docs, consistent JSDoc, green docs build.

## Risks

- Documenting an assumption as fact — the competitive human-seat scope must be
  labelled as the current working assumption until the producer confirms.

# End-of-game stats acceptance verification

Parent: MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV — End of game stats (phase 6, verification).

## Goal (user story)

As the producer, I want one end-to-end acceptance test proving the whole
end-of-game stats story (capture → persist → model → render) works in both
modes, plus a mapping from every parent acceptance criterion to its evidence,
so the epic can be reviewed without trusting individual child claims.

## Scope

- **In:** a scripted end-to-end acceptance test in both modes, the parent
  AC → evidence mapping, full-suite green evidence.
- **Out:** new features; gaps large enough to need their own scope (record as
  `discovered-from:MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV` items).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes** via
   `/skill:test --scope full`.
2. **Single-player acceptance.** A new test drives a scripted multi-turn
   single-player run through the real engine (`executeFullTurn`), then asserts:
   exactly one history entry per completed turn, `profit` equals the coin delta
   against the day-start snapshot, `serializeMainStreetState` →
   `deserializeMainStreetState` preserves the series, and
   `buildGameOverStatSeries` yields five series with matching point counts and
   the correct `finalCash`.
3. **Competitive acceptance.** The same test drives a scripted competitive run
   and asserts one history entry per turn from the human seat and a series
   model that matches it.
4. **AC traceability.** A comment on the parent maps each parent acceptance
   criterion (1–9) to the test file/test name or document that evidences it,
   and flags any criterion still unproven; the green full-suite run is recorded
   and cached for the audit.
5. **Gaps handled.** Any gap found is either fixed inline (minimal, in-scope) or
   recorded as a `discovered-from:MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV` work item and referenced
   in the AC mapping comment.

## Minimal implementation

1. `tests/main-street/end-of-game-stats-acceptance.test.ts` — scripted engine
   runs + round-trip + series assertions, single-player and competitive.
2. Parent comment: AC → evidence table.
3. Test-skill full run; triage any failure per the triage policy.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `tests/main-street/end-of-game-stats-acceptance.test.ts` — **new**.
- `tests/main-street/turn-stats-history.test.ts` — reused fixtures/helpers.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-game-over-stats.test.ts` — reused competitive
  fixture.

## Dependencies

Blocked by every earlier child (capture/model, chart spike, third column,
competitive/both-mode, docs).

## Deliverables

Acceptance test, AC-to-evidence mapping comment, full-suite green evidence.

## Risks

- Scripted runs may be flaky if engine randomness leaks into assertions — pin
  seeds and assert invariants (counts, deltas) rather than exact coin values
  where randomness applies.
